pages.title: Build Your First Page on systeme.io | SoloStarter HQ
pages.desc: A step-by-step guide to building your first page or funnel on systeme.io's free plan: pick a template, edit it, connect payments and publish.
pages.h1: Build your first page on systeme.io, step by step
pages.card: From a blank account to a published page, using systeme.io's own steps.
pages.lede: The quickest way to see whether systeme.io suits you is to publish something real. This guide follows systeme.io's own steps for a first funnel and a first website, both of which work on the free plan.

p: You need a free systeme.io account. systeme.io says the free plan "never expires and does not require a credit card", so there is nothing to cancel if you decide it isn't for you.

Decide what your first page is for. For most freelancers it is one of two things: a simple website that explains what you do, or a single page that collects email addresses or sells one offer. systeme.io calls the second kind a sales funnel.

systeme.io describes a sales funnel as "a sequence of pages that guides a visitor from their first contact with your business to a purchase", typically an opt-in page, a sales page, a checkout page and a thank-you page. The free plan includes up to 3 funnels.
ol: Go to Funnels in your dashboard and click "Create a funnel".
Choose a funnel type (lead capture, product sales, webinar and so on) and pick a template.
Click each step to edit the page in the drag-and-drop editor: change the text, images and offer details.
If you are selling, connect your payment processor on the checkout step.
Set up an email automation to follow up with new leads or buyers.
sections.after: systeme.io says most first funnels can be live in under 2 hours.

p: The website builder is included on the free plan. systeme.io describes the process as: choose a template, customise text and images, add pages, set up navigation, configure your domain, and publish, with no coding needed.
ul: Start from a ready-made template, then change colours, fonts and images across the whole site.
Add pages such as Home, Services and Contact, and arrange your navigation menu.
Set the title and description each page shows on Google in its settings.
Publish on your own domain: the free plan includes 1 custom domain.

sections.h2: Connect it to your email list
p: Whichever option you choose, add a form. systeme.io says that when a visitor fills in a form on your website or funnel, they are added to your contacts automatically, ready for email follow-up. That is the start of an email list you own.
Once your page is live, the next useful steps are a welcome email for new subscribers and, if you sell services, a booking page. The guides below cover both.

faq: Do I need to know how to code?
No. systeme.io says its editor is entirely visual: you click any element to edit it and drag blocks to reorder them. Custom CSS is possible for advanced users but never required.
Can I use my own domain on the free plan?
Yes. systeme.io's pricing page lists 1 custom domain on the free plan.
Can I take payments on the free plan?
Yes. systeme.io says you connect a payment processor such as Stripe or PayPal on the checkout step, and it charges 0% transaction fees on every plan. Your payment processor's own fees still apply.

pages.title: systeme.io Free Plan: What You Get, Limits | SoloStarter HQ
pages.desc: What systeme.io's free plan includes, from 2,000 contacts and unlimited emails to 3 funnels and 1 course, and the limits to know before you start.
pages.h1: The systeme.io free plan: what you get, and the limits
pages.card: Exactly what's included for free, and where the limits are.
pages.lede: systeme.io's free plan covers a lot, but it does have limits. Here is what systeme.io says it includes, in its own figures, so you know what you can do before you pay anything.

p: According to systeme.io's pricing page, the free plan includes:
ul: Up to 2,000 contacts
Unlimited email sends
3 sales funnels
1 blog
1 course
1 affiliate program
1 custom domain
1 automation rule and 1 email campaign
sections.after: systeme.io also says every plan includes unlimited sub-accounts, 0% transaction fees and "the same set of core tools".

p: systeme.io says the free plan "never expires and does not require a credit card". It is not a time-limited trial: you can stay on it for as long as your business fits within its limits.
For most freelancers starting out, two limits decide when you outgrow the free plan:
ul: Contacts: the free plan stops at 2,000. systeme.io's plans are "based primarily on contact limits".

Automation: the free plan includes 1 automation rule and 1 email campaign. If you want several separate email sequences, for example one for each product, you will reach this limit before the contact limit.
sections.after: Funnels (3) and courses (1) are the other limits to watch if you sell more than one thing.

p: systeme.io's own advice is simple: "Under 2,000 contacts: use the free plan. It costs nothing and covers most needs." For a freelancer with a portfolio site, a newsletter and one offer, that usually means you can run on the free plan for a long time.

faq: Is the systeme.io free plan really free forever?
systeme.io says the free plan never expires and does not require a credit card.
How many emails can I send on the free plan?
Unlimited. systeme.io says there is no daily or monthly send cap; the number of contacts (2,000 on the free plan) is the only constraint.
Does systeme.io take a cut of my sales on the free plan?
No. systeme.io charges 0% transaction fees on every plan, including the free plan. Your payment processor (for example Stripe or PayPal) still charges its own fees.

pages.title: When Is a Paid systeme.io Plan Worth It? | SoloStarter HQ
pages.desc: systeme.io's paid plans compared: Startup, Webinar and Unlimited, what each adds over the free plan, and how to tell when it's time to upgrade.
pages.h1: When is a paid systeme.io plan worth it?
pages.card: The signs you've outgrown the free plan, and which plan comes next.
pages.lede: Start free and upgrade when your business needs it. This guide sets out what each paid plan adds, using systeme.io's own figures, so you can tell when the jump is worth making.

sections.h2: The four plans at a glance
p: systeme.io's pricing page lists four plans, "based primarily on contact limits":
ul: Free: 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, 1 course.
Startup ($17 a month): 5,000 contacts, 10 sales funnels, 5 courses.
Webinar ($47 a month): 10,000 contacts, 50 sales funnels, 20 courses, plus evergreen webinars.
Unlimited ($97 a month): unlimited contacts, funnels, courses and automation rules.
sections.after: All plans include unlimited email sends, unlimited sub-accounts and 0% transaction fees. Paying yearly gives you 2 months free, according to the pricing page.

ul: Your list is close to 2,000 contacts. systeme.io's own advice: "2,000 to 5,000 contacts: Startup at $17/month."
You need more than one email campaign or automation rule, the free plan's tightest limits.
You want to sell more than one course or run more than three funnels.
You want automated webinars, which start on the Webinar plan.

p: systeme.io says you can upgrade or cancel at any time from your account settings. If you cancel, you keep your current plan until your next billing date, then your account reverts to the free plan, so your account carries on rather than disappearing.

If you are moving an existing business from another platform, systeme.io offers a free done-for-you migration with the Unlimited monthly plan or any annual plan. It says its team moves funnels, pages, email lists and sequences, courses and customer records for you.

faq: What does the systeme.io Startup plan cost?
systeme.io lists the Startup plan at $17 a month, with 5,000 contacts, 10 sales funnels and 5 courses. Paying annually gives 2 months free.
What happens if I cancel a paid plan?
systeme.io says you keep your current plan until the next billing date, then your account reverts to the free plan.
Is the free migration really free?
systeme.io says there is no extra fee for the migration service, which is included with the Unlimited monthly plan or any annual plan.

A paid template, guide or mini-course with a checkout page.
A discovery-call funnel that ends on your booking page.

pages.title: systeme.io Automation: Save Freelance Time | SoloStarter HQ
pages.desc: How systeme.io's automation rules and workflows work: triggers, actions, tags, delays and email sequences, and what the free plan includes.
pages.h1: Automations that save a freelancer time
pages.card: Let the system send emails, tag contacts and give access for you.
pages.lede: Automation means the routine follow-up happens without you. systeme.io has two kinds: simple rules and visual workflows, both built in.

p: systeme.io describes two tools. Automation rules are simple if-then pairs: a trigger such as "Form subscribed" with an action such as "Subscribe to campaign". Workflows are visual, multi-step flows that can include delays, conditions and branching.

systeme.io lists triggers such as signing up, making a purchase, clicking a link, a tag being added or a date. Actions include sending emails, giving course access, updating tags and moving someone to a different funnel.

ul: Someone downloads your free checklist: tag them and start a welcome sequence.
Someone buys your template: send the download and a follow-up email a few days later.
Someone books a call: tag them as a lead so they get the right newsletters.

p: The pricing page lists 1 automation rule on the free plan, and unlimited automation rules on the Unlimited plan. If automation is central to your business, check which plan you need on systeme.io's pricing page.

faq: Do I need to code to build automations?
No. systeme.io says its workflow builder uses drag-and-drop blocks, with no coding or API keys.
How many automation rules are on the free plan?
systeme.io's pricing page lists 1 automation rule on the free plan.
Can automations give access to a course?
Yes. systeme.io lists granting course access among the actions a rule or workflow can take.

pages.title: Why systeme.io Can Replace Several Tools | SoloStarter HQ
pages.desc: Why systeme.io's all-in-one approach suits freelancers: pages, email, courses, bookings, automation and payments in one account sharing one contact list.
pages.h1: Why one tool can replace several
pages.card: One account and one contact list, instead of a stack of subscriptions.
pages.lede: Many freelancers pay for a website builder, an email tool, a course platform and a booking app, then spend time connecting them. systeme.io's pitch is that one account does all of this. Here is what it includes, in its own words.

p: systeme.io lists these among its features: sales funnels, email marketing, a website builder, marketing automation, online courses, a booking calendar, affiliate management, communities and evergreen webinars. Its pricing page says all plans include "the same set of core tools".

sections.h2: Why it matters: one contact list
p: systeme.io says "every feature in systeme.io works together". Because email, tags, funnels, courses and contacts live in the same system, a sign-up, purchase or booking lands in one contact list, and one automation can send emails, give course access and move people between funnels. systeme.io says this means you don't need to sync data between separate tools.
systeme.io says it covers a typical stack of separate funnel, email, course and affiliate tools on the free plan or for $17 a month, and that every plan has 0% transaction fees.

systeme.io itself says some specialist tools go further in places: more advanced email design, more website templates, advanced team scheduling, and course certificates, which it doesn't offer natively. If one of those is essential to you, check it before you switch.

faq: Does systeme.io replace a separate email tool?
For email inside your own business, systeme.io says yes: email is built into the same account as your funnels and courses. Specialist email tools may have more advanced design features.
Can I move my existing business to systeme.io?
Yes. systeme.io offers a free migration with the Unlimited monthly plan or any annual plan.
Is there a catch with the free plan?
The main limits are 2,000 contacts, 1 email campaign and 1 automation rule. The free plan never expires and needs no credit card.
